item.title: Legendary Las Vegas buffet to close for renovations after rumors swirled of its demise
item.description: Caesars Palace's Bacchanal Buffet in Las Vegas is closing Jan. 4, 2027, for a major renovation of its dessert area and five specialty kitchens. It's expected to reopen in the summer.
item.content:encoded:
Visitors planning a trip to Las Vegas in the near future will miss out on one of the Strip's best-known all-you-can-eat destinations, at least temporarily.

Caesars Palace announced Nov. 18 that its Bacchanal Buffet will temporarily close on Monday, Jan. 4, 2027, for a major renovation, according to a news release shared with Fox News Digital.

The closure is expected to last until summer 2027, the hotel said.

BARGAIN BUFFET REFUSES TO DIE WHILE LUXURY DINING TAKES OVER VEGAS

Diners hoping to visit before construction starts have until Sunday, Jan. 3, to dine at the venue.

The upcoming project marks the second restoration for the 25,000-square-foot dining hall since it opened in September 2012, the resort said.

While a 2021 remodel updated several sections, the 2027 renovation will focus on the dessert area and five specialty kitchens serving Italian, Mediterranean, Asian grill and barbecue, sushi and sashimi, and regional Asian dishes, the press release said.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Caesars Palace said the updates will bring new menu options and dining experiences to the Strip venue.

"We’re doubling down on Bacchanal Buffet with this renovation," Terrence O’Donnell, senior vice president and general manager of Caesars Palace, said in the release.

"This next chapter brings fresh flavors and new experiences to the buffet, giving guests even more to look forward to when we welcome them back next summer," O'Donnell added.

The redesign will incorporate wood counters and shelving, brushed-metal finishes and illuminated onyx panels at the dessert station, the company said. 

News of the months-long shutdown quickly drew mixed reactions among frequent Las Vegas visitors.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"Bacchanal is the first name out of everyone's mouth when someone asks about a Vegas buffet, so a renovation closure is going to surprise a lot of people booking winter trips," one Reddit user wrote.

"I think this is horrible news," another user wrote.

Others wondered why a partial remodel would take six months or so. 

Some even questioned if the buffet would ever reopen.

"I have that fear myself. Six months seems like too long of a time for some minor renovations," another person replied.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Some Vegas fans pointed out, however, that extended construction timelines are standard on the Strip.

"Lengthy renovations are nothing new in Vegas. The question is how much of an improvement it will be," the commenter wrote.

As Fox News Digital reported this past summer, many of the famous buffets of Las Vegas fell victim in recent years to the COVID-19 pandemic, its social-distancing requirements and the trend of wealthier visitors seeking out higher-end restaurants.

There were over a dozen traditional Vegas buffets on the Strip in 2020, The Wall Street Journal reported. 

Now, there are just a handful.  

Unlike many Strip resorts, budget casinos rely heavily on repeat local customers and value-conscious gamblers, making inexpensive buffets an effective way to drive casino traffic.

Fox News Digital reached out to Caesars Palace for additional information.

Theresa Mull contributed reporting.

item.title: Cowboys great Michael Irvin outlines franchise's timeline to retain 'America’s Team' status
item.description: Michael Irvin says Jerry Jones' Dallas Cowboys have about 10 years to win a Super Bowl before losing the "America's Team" title to another NFC team.
item.content:encoded:
More than three decades have passed since the Dallas Cowboys last advanced to a Super Bowl. In the years since, the franchise has experienced limited postseason success and has not returned to the NFC Championship Game.

Even so, the Cowboys remain one of the NFL’s most popular teams, frequently appearing in nationally televised windows and routinely drawing prime time interest. Their history, including five Super Bowl titles, which rank second among NFL teams, has helped the franchise retain its widely recognized "America’s Team" moniker.

However, Cowboys Ring of Honor member Michael Irvin says the popular nickname should be retired unless Dallas starts winning.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Irvin was a key part of the Cowboys’ three Super Bowl-winning teams in the 1990s, a run that built on the "America's Team" status. The retired wide receiver is giving his former team a decade-long runway to prove it should keep the label.

COWBOYS LEGEND DIGS DEEP INTO THE TEAM'S MISSING 'FIBER' THAT'S RESULTED IN SUPER BOWL DROUGHT

"A whole generation goes by and never experiences the glory of a championship story from the Dallas Cowboys," Irvin told CNBC on Thursday. "A generation is considered 40 years in the bible. So the Cowboys got about 10 years [to win a Super Bowl and keep the 'America’s Team' title]."

Irvin wore the famed "star" on the side of his helmet for his entire NFL career and was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2007. He finished his career with more than 11,000 regular season receiving yards.

The Cowboys have missed the postseason in each of the past two seasons and could face another early offseason this year. Dallas is competing in an uneven NFC East, with the Philadelphia Eagles dealing with notable injuries and the Washington Commanders struggling.

COWBOYS STAR QUINNEN WILLIAMS REPEATS SIX WORD ANSWER 12 TIMES IN PRESSER AFTER MAJOR COACHING CHANGE

After the Cowboys' defense faltered again in a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers last Sunday, defensive coordinator Christian Parker was relieved of his play-calling duties. The Cowboys enter Sunday’s game against the 1-8 Tennessee Titans at 4-6, needing a win to keep their playoff hopes alive.

Parker, 34, spent the previous two seasons as the Eagles passing game coordinator & defensive backs coach.

In the the 10 games he's handled defensive playcalling for Dallas, the team ranks 32 in the NFL in total yards allowed and rushing yards given up. The 49ers put up 584 yards against Dallas in Week 10, the most the Cowboys’ defense has allowed in a home game in franchise history.

item.title: Hasan Piker complains the far-left has less leverage on Democratic Party because the Dems won too many seats
item.description: Hasan Piker lamented Democrats' vast midterm margin weakened the far-left's leverage, saying a smaller win could have let socialists pressure the party.
item.content:encoded:
Far-left streamer Hasan Piker lamented that the Democrats were so successful in the midterms that they aren’t as dependent on their far-left flank.

The Democrats won a resounding victory in the midterms which surprised not only the Republican Party, but the far-left. Just a month before the midterms, Piker had talked about using the far-left to pressure then-candidate James Talarico to push progressive policy, saying, "We are the force that allowed him to win this seat of power and if he wants to maintain it, he’s got to play ball."

On Wednesday night, however, Piker played a different tune, noting that the Democratic Party was so successful that it is no longer as dependent on support from its most left-wing members.

"I think that there was a way that we could possibly get out of this fight with clear concessions on our agenda. We didn't. Part of that was because nobody expected the margin to be so vast!" he said. "If the margin was 10, then we could have made an impact. If the Democratic Party's margin of victory was 10 and not like f---ing 40, okay, then yeah, we could have had a big caucus, a socialist caucus, a fighter caucus, whatever you want to call it, that could potentially bully the party to be more responsive to the needs of the masses."

HASAN PIKER DECLARES 'WOKE IS BACK,' FANTASIZES ABOUT PUTTING DONALD TRUMP IN PRISON

Piker also hit back at some critical comments from his fans.

"’This is you at your worst,'" he read aloud one comment before responding. "Why? Because I have to explain to you as an adult who is a political pundit how, you know, how change never really happens in Washington, D.C.? It hurts your feelings to hear someone explain to you why these things happen while simultaneously telling you how much I oppose it? Does it hurt your feelings to hear how this goes?" he asked. "It's just reality."

"I'm going to continue to explain how the sausage gets made, even if that hurts your f---ing feelings, because you're too dumb to understand," he said.

Republican consultant Mary Marslender reacted to Piker's commentary.

"Hasan Piker is furious that Democrats won too many seats because it weakened the DSA’s ability to hold the Democratic Party hostage. Piker’s complaint reveals that the far-left prefers narrow majorities so it can force its destructive socialist experiments on our country and European-style street chaos," she told Fox News Digital.

FAR-LEFT STREAMER HASAN PIKER GLOATS AFTER DEM BLOWOUT, PROMISES ‘JAIL’ FOR CONSERVATIVE ENEMIES

Democratic strategist and co-host of "The Huddle" podcast Dan Turrentine told Fox News Digital, "There is the world as Hasan Piker wished it would be, and the real world. Socialists are utterly irrelevant in the next Congress. They are not the majority of America, nor are they the majority of the Democratic Party. In fact, in the next Congress, Socialists will be a tiny 2.7% of the House Democratic caucus and there will be only one in the Senate, Bernie Sanders."

item.title: Baltimore DC Anthony Weaver addresses Marlon Humphrey 1-game banishment over city crime remarks
item.description: Anthony Weaver backed Marlon Humphrey's benching, saying freedom of speech doesn't mean freedom of consequence after the Ravens star's podcast remarks.
item.content:encoded:
Baltimore Ravens defensive coordinator Anthony Weaver backed the franchise Thursday after head coach Jesse Minter sent veteran cornerback Marlon Humphrey home and benched him for Sunday's game against Carolina.

Humphrey is a healthy scratch for claiming on his podcast that Baltimore is "best at making criminals." Even after Humphrey apologized Wednesday, Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott dismissed the remarks as "not enough" before Minter stepped in.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

The controversy has also highlighted a glaring double standard in Baltimore: wide receiver Rashod Bateman continues to play despite facing offseason family violence charges, while franchise icon Ray Lewis is honored outside the stadium with a statue.

RAVENS' RASHOD BATEMAN FACES DOMESTIC CHARGES FOR ALLEGED ATTACK ON CAR CARRYING EX-GIRLFRIEND AND THEIR BABY

Stepping to the podium Thursday, Weaver backed Humphrey's benching.

"This is a learning moment," Weaver said. "In this day and age, I think it's important for these guys to understand that, yes, you have freedom of speech. You can say what it is you want to say, on your phone, on your platform, whatever that is. But that doesn't give you freedom of consequence."

RAVENS PLAYERS RIDE WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP IN MOTORCADE, GET SHOUTOUT DURING SPEECH AT BALTIMORE SHIPYARD EVENT

"I think that's where we're at," Weaver added. "So, we're living in that, regardless of intent. He said the things that he said, which obviously is negative toward where we live and where we love."

Even while endorsing the benching, Weaver distinguished between Humphrey's character and his poor judgment.

MARLON HUMPHREY SAYS MEETING PRESIDENT TRUMP INSPIRED HIM TO VOTE IN THE NEXT ELECTION

"I think as a dad, as a coach, as a Christian, it's important to say that I can love the man, have respect for him, and disagree with what he said in this particular moment," Weaver said.

Running a podcast is easier when you are actually playing well, and Humphrey hasn't been.

"I think it's safe to say that, defensively, we haven't lived up to our standard," Weaver admitted. "So, as it pertains to him individually, I think a lot of his errors have been a product of technique and fundamentals."

"That's weird to say for a guy that's been at his stature for such a long time, but it's one of those things where you're constantly sharpening and making sure your tires are aligned as a player."

"It's very easy to get comfortable and start to let those things go by the wayside a little bit," Weaver said. "When that happens, you give up plays like that. Particularly as you age, you're just not able to rely on your pure athleticism, maybe as you once did."

item.title: Trump clears hurdle in $15 billion lawsuit against New York Times
item.description: President Donald Trump’s legal team celebrated Thursday after a judge denied The New York Times’ motion to dismiss a $15 billion defamation lawsuit against the paper.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump’s legal team is celebrating Thursday after a judge denied The New York Times’ motion to dismiss the president’s $15 billion defamation lawsuit against the paper.

U.S. District Judge Steven D. Merryday allowed four counts centered on seven specific accusations of criminal conduct to move forward after Trump’s legal team argued that the Times and publisher Penguin Random House showed reckless disregard, alleging "purposeful avoidance of the truth" in a book authored by Times journalists.

"President Trump continues holding the Fake News accountable for deceiving the American people. Judge Merryday has correctly denied the motion to dismiss filed by The New York Times, Penguin Publishing and their writers as to President Trump’s powerhouse defamation lawsuit," a spokesman for Trump’s legal team told Fox News Digital.

NEW YORK TIMES LOSES DEFAMATION SUIT, ORDERED TO PAY $9.25M TO FORMER ALABAMA BASKETBALL PLAYER

"These defendants will now have to answer for intentionally and maliciously defaming President Trump," the spokesman continued. "The New York Times has a long pattern of defaming President Trump in service of its leftist political agenda, and today’s momentous ruling is a victory for honesty in America."

Judge Merryday issued a pointed critique of Susanne Craig and Russ Buettner, the authors of "Lucky Loser: How Donald Trump Squandered His Father’s Fortune and Created the Illusion of Success," for publishing definitive claims of complex tax fraud and money laundering without a formal legal opinion or forensic auditing.

Merryday observed that accusations were made against Trump and his father without charges or convictions.

"In other words, the facts alleged in the complaint create at least a plausible inference that the authors and the publishers knew that no reliable conclusion about violations of the tax laws, including especially the estate and gift tax laws, is possible without reliance on qualified opinion formulated after the necessary factual and legal research and analysis, which they knowingly failed to obtain," Merryday wrote.

TRUMP TOUTS LEGAL VICTORY OVER BBC AS JUDGE SAYS HIS LAWSUIT AGAINST BRITISH BROADCASTER CAN PROCEED

The court dismissed the Times’ reliance on outside commentators, such as a former prosecutor saying a Trump transaction "smells like a crime" and a professor who called the action "suspicious."

"Obviously, even a qualified expert offering a superficial characterization such as a transaction is ‘suspicious’ or ‘could’ violate the law or attributing to a transaction the ‘smell’ of crime or noting that a gift tax return can evade IRS scrutiny or generously giving his immensely valuable time to aid laypersons ‘lost in the weeds’ is far from a formal legal opinion sufficient to remove serious doubt about the truthfulness and accuracy of a statement accusing a specific person of fraud or tax evasion or some related crime arising from a specific transaction," Merryday wrote.

While Trump’s lawsuit can move forward, Merryday also dismissed two counts and threw out 27 other challenged statements as non-actionable under the strict First Amendment protections of New York Times Co. v. Sullivan and denied Trump's request to amend his complaint a third time.

TRUMP DOJ WITHDRAWS SUBPOENAS TARGETING NEW YORK TIMES JOURNALISTS AMID LEAK PROBE

A New York Times spokesperson provided the following statement to Fox News Digital: "The Times is encouraged to see Judge Merryday’s dismissal of almost all claims against us. We continue to believe the remaining claim in the filing has no legal merit. We look forward to making this argument as we continue to defend ourselves against this baseless attack on The Times and the rights of the free and independent press in this country."

The judge ordered The New York Times to file a formal answer within 28 days.

Fox News Digital’s Joseph A. Wulfsohn contributed to this report.

item.title: House China panel calls for cutting defense contracts over aerospace ties to Beijing's military
item.description: A new House report says Airbus and U.S. defense contractors like GE Aerospace and Honeywell should lose taxpayer funds over China aerospace joint ventures.
item.content:encoded:
A new congressional report is urging the U.S. to restrict investments in China’s aerospace sector and withhold taxpayer funding from companies that build military capabilities for U.S. adversaries, warning that Western commercial partnerships transferred technology and expertise to Chinese firms with military ties.

The 65-page report, titled "China's Wingmen: How Western Government Policy Enabled China's Rise in the Skies," follows a year-long investigation by the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party, led by Chairman John Moolenaar, R-Mich., and Ranking Member Ro Khanna, D-Calif. It examined how legal commercial partnerships transferred advanced technology and manufacturing expertise to Chinese military-linked companies.

China's People's Liberation Army (PLA) is the country's military, which the committee says has benefited from civilian aerospace technology transfers.

"American and European companies transferred technology to China that could be used against our brave men and women in uniform. With the CCP’s military-civil fusion there are no private companies in China," Moolenaar said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital.

CHINA COULD EXPLOIT US TECHNOLOGY TO THREATEN AMERICAN FORCES, CONGRESSIONAL WATCHDOG LEADERS WARN

"The PLA will exploit civilian technology and use it to advance its military ambitions and that is what happened here."

The report singled out European aerospace giant Airbus, which receives U.S. defense contracts while maintaining manufacturing partnerships in China. Although Airbus sold its stake in an AVIC affiliate in 2025, its commercial partnerships with the Chinese aerospace conglomerate continue, according to the committee.

The bipartisan panel examined at least six U.S.-China joint ventures involving American defense suppliers GE Aerospace, Honeywell Aerospace and RTX subsidiary Collins Aerospace.

Investigators found that GE transferred foundational avionics technology to a joint venture with a subsidiary of AVIC, the Chinese state-owned conglomerate that develops military aircraft, including the J-20 stealth fighter. The committee said GE withheld its original joint venture agreement despite repeated requests.

RUSSIA IS HELPING CHINA CLOSE GAP WITH US FORCES AMID TAIWAN TENSIONS, WARNS LONGTIME MILITARY LEADER

The American companies maintained that their Chinese partnerships supported civilian aircraft and complied with U.S. export controls. The report also cited previous export-control settlements involving all three companies but did not establish that the partnerships under investigation violated U.S. law.

"We appreciate the Committee’s work ensuring the U.S. retains its position as the world’s commercial aviation leader while protecting our most sensitive technologies. We have and will continue to follow relevant U.S. laws and regulations, as the report acknowledges,"a Collins Aerospace spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

The committee urged the Federal Aviation Administration not to certify Chinese-manufactured aircraft, citing state subsidies and Beijing's refusal to release a final report on the 2022 China Eastern Airlines crash.

"The report’s only recommendation directed at the FAA is that they do not certify Chinese-made aircraft, which the agency has not done," an FAA spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

A representative for Airbus did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Teen accused of fatally shooting identical twin brother after fight about touching his belongings
item.description: Jamari Young, 16, was arrested in the Washington, D.C., shooting death of his identical twin brother, Jabrell Young. U.S. Marshals took Jamari into custody.
item.content:encoded:
A teenage boy was arrested Wednesday in the fatal shooting of his identical twin brother inside their Washington, D.C., home after an argument, police said.

The U.S. Marshals Service took 16-year-old Jamari Young into custody, according to the Metropolitan Police Department. He was charged as an adult with second-degree murder while armed. 

On Thursday, a judge ordered the teen held without bond.

Family members told affiliate FOX 5 DC they turned Young in to authorities after the Oct. 25 death of his brother, Jabrell Young, also 16.

TEEN ARRESTED IN GIRL'S MURDER ONE YEAR AFTER POLICE SAID SHE ACCIDENTALLY SHOT HERSELF WHILE RECORDING VIDEO

Officers responding to the home that day found Jabrell unconscious and not breathing. He was pronounced dead inside the home, where he died in his mother's arms, relatives said.

Prior to the shooting, the brothers had been in an argument over Jabrell going into Jamari's room and touching his belongings, according to court documents obtained by the news outlet. As the boys' mother applied pressure to Jabrell's wounds in an effort to save his life, Jamari allegedly said, "I didn’t mean to. It just went off. I didn’t mean to. I’m sorry, Ma."

The twins' mother allegedly yelled at her son to leave the house after the shooting. Neighborhood security cameras showed Jamari walking and then running from the neighborhood.

Detectives investigated the death as a homicide, and a search for Jamari was launched.

Authorities found two .45-caliber shell casings inside the house but have yet to recover the weapon used in the killing.

GET BREAKING NEWS ALERTS

After the shooting, someone in the home allegedly tossed a blanket under a nearby parked car, where officers found a 9 mm pistol inside that was traced to an unsolved fatal shooting in July, FOX 5 reported.

Authorities have not confirmed who tossed the blanket under the parked car. Investigators also have not disclosed where Jamari went after leaving the residence or whether he was given assistance while missing.

The twins' aunt told the news outlet that the shooting was accidental, saying Jamari was terrified and had not intended to shoot his brother.

After Thursday's court hearing, the boys' mother said her sons were inseparable and that the shooting was an accident.

TEEN ARRESTED ON MURDER CHARGES AFTER CITADEL CADET AND CHILDHOOD FRIEND FOUND SHOT DEAD

"This is an accident. This is an accident, but they're putting out a narrative that my son is just a monster and that this is something that was just malicious," she told FOX 5. "This is not malicious, sir. My son and his brother are best friends. They love each other. Ride or die."

She added that she feels her family has been targeted by law enforcement.

"I've been harassed. I've been stalked. I've been threatened. I've been mistreated. My family has been mistreated since day one," she said. "I've been treated like I'm the suspect. I haven't been treated like I'm a grieving mom. I've been treated like I'm the one whose [at] fault for all this."

In an online fundraiser, the twins' mother said Jamari was "being portrayed in a way that could put his life in danger."

She said investigators took all of her electronic devices and that "i continue to face legal pressure while i am still trying to grieve and find the strength to get through each day," according to the fundraiser, which had raised more than $1,200 for the family as of Thursday afternoon.

item.title: 49ers' Kyle Juszczyk reveals hardest part of playing in Mexico City as San Fran returns to face Vikings
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers trained at the Air Force Academy to adapt to Mexico City's thin air before facing the Minnesota Vikings on "Sunday Night Football."
item.content:encoded:
Earlier this season, the San Francisco 49ers seemed to gain an edge in their game-week prep by flying down to Australia while the Los Angeles Rams stayed home.

In Week 11, as the 49ers and Minnesota Vikings head down to Mexico City for yet another NFL international matchup, they are hoping for an edge to prepare for a different challenge this time.

It isn’t a time difference, but rather a massive elevation difference in Mexico City. The capital of Mexico sits 7,350 feet above sea level, which is roughly 2,000 feet higher than Denver, Colorado, known as the Mile High City.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

So, the 49ers have been preparing for this week against a tough Minnesota opponent at the Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs to get acclimated to the thin air. Fullback Kyle Juszczyk, who was a member of the 49ers when they thrashed the Arizona Cardinals four years ago in Mexico City, believes his team’s strategy is sound considering his experience.

"I think just being here a week early is going to help a lot," he told OutKick during a recent interview. "Just training in it, sleeping in it — just being in it for a week. Definitely gives you at least an opportunity to feel what that feels like and let your body adapt. We did the same thing, I think it was four years ago, when we played in Mexico City. We had a good result. We won the game pretty big against Arizona. So, hoping for the same thing this week."

Juszczyk knows, though, that Mexico City’s air is going to be a struggle even with the training.

"The hardest thing was getting back into the locker room. We went down, we did our warm-ups. Felt pretty good, but the stadium in Mexico City I just remember to get back to our locker room was a long walk and the incline was like 45 degrees. I just remember that was the hardest part of the entire game, just getting back to the locker room after warm-ups and at halftime," he recalled, laughing.

On the other hand, the Vikings are remaining at home this week before traveling, as they have built a high-altitude room at their facility.

They have been doing simulated workouts with roster rotations inside this room for weeks, with players getting acclimated to simulated altitudes that have been gradually raised to get them familiar with what’s in store below the border.

Which strategy will work best: The 49ers’ in real-life elevation, or the Vikings’ simulated altitude at home?

From experience, Juszczyk knows what worked well last time out. Much like that game in Australia, "Sunday Night Football" will be the decider of which strategy works best between these two NFC contenders.

item.title: Human vs. ChatGPT NFL Week 11 betting picks: A struggling human backs ugly underdogs to stop the slide
item.description: A 4-11 skid leaves the human searching for answers, while ChatGPT enters NFL Week 11 with two straight winning cards and a chance to erase a shrinking deficit.
item.content:encoded:
If I wasn’t officially ice cold entering Week 10, I certainly am entering Week 11. After another losing week (2-3, -1.33 units), I am now 4-11 and down 8.52 units since the start of Week 8.

But there is good news. As someone who publicly posts betting picks on the internet, I’ve often said that you either need to be really good or really bad. If you’re really good, people can follow your picks and make money. If you’re really bad, people can fade your picks and make money. If you’re just average, then you basically just lose the juice and cost everyone money. That’s the worst-case scenario.

ONE WILD WEEK 11 BETTING STAT SHOWS JUST HOW FAR APART THE NFL’S BEST AND WORST TEAMS ARE

Right now, I might be one of the best on the internet at providing fadable NFL picks. And that’s something. It’s not great for me. But it’s good for you. And my No. 1 priority is the audience, so you know what? It’s good for me, too.

Both of us get five selections from the same odds board, with no bet priced worse than -120. Odds were taken from the board supplied Thursday at 4 p.m. ET.

Stakes are adjusted so every winning bet produces one unit of profit. For example, -110 requires risking 1.10 units, while +110 requires approximately 0.91 units. A push returns the stake and counts as zero units.

Washington won outright on Thursday Night Football, and the Dolphins-Colts over got us another winner. I thought I was headed toward a winning week, but Drake Maye suffered a potentially season-ending ankle injury in the first quarter against Detroit (not the first time a team we bet on lost its quarterback in the first 15 minutes of a game).

Then, the Texans had a 17-0 lead and blew it against the CLEVELAND BROWNS. That pretty much sums up my season. Actually, the Steelers falling into a 31-3 hole against the Bengals probably sums it up better.

WHICH NFL TEAMS CAN ACTUALLY WIN THE SUPER BOWL? RANKING ALL 32 AT THE SEASON’S HALFWAY POINT

GPT went 3-2 for the second straight week and picked up another 0.77 units. The Chiefs and Bills covered comfortably, while the Vikings and Packers stayed under the total. The 49ers and Cowboys combined for 86 points, so that was a bad miss.

Then it joined me on Pittsburgh. I was right about one thing: "Theoretically, I should be more confident now, but suddenly I'm worried. That can't be good, right?" That's what I wrote when GPT spit out the same Pittsburgh pick that I had. I guess I was right that I was probably going to be wrong.

DAN: 23-26-1, -5.32 units

GPT: 22-27-1, -6.90 units

I still lead GPT by 1.58 units, although bragging about losing less money than a robot probably tells you everything you need to know about how this season is going.

Dan Z.’s Plug Your Nose and Hit ‘Place Bet’ Bet of the Week: 6-3, +2.83 units

At least the Plug Your Nose bet is making money. Maybe the problem is that I’m only picking one of those per week.

Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

Dan’s analysis:

Nothing says "let’s turn this season around" like betting on the Tennessee Titans. But this is the kind of ugly underdog I want to be backing. Tennessee has scored at least 23 points in four straight games, while Dallas ranks last in yards allowed and 30th in scoring defense. Changing the defensive play-caller to Mike Pettine shows how desperate the Cowboys are to adjust, but Pettine doesn't magically help the personnel get better.

That makes Tennessee this week’s Dan Z.’s Plug Your Nose and Hit ‘Place Bet’ Bet of the Week. The name continues to do a lot of work.

GPT’s analysis:

We’re on the same side. Tennessee has scored at least 23 points in four straight games, and Dallas allows a league-worst 154.1 rushing yards per game. I paid for +9½ because the Titans can lose 31-23 and still cash. That score pushes your bet, but I like getting better than a touchdown at -108.

Pittsburgh Steelers at Philadelphia Eagles, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET

Dan’s analysis:

The Steelers embarrassed us on Sunday Night Football, and now I’m laying points with them on the road. Apparently, I just hate myself.

But getting blown out by Cincinnati doesn’t suddenly make Pittsburgh a bad team. The Steelers are still 6-3, while Philadelphia is 2-7 and starting Joe Milton III for the second time. item.title: Locals of Michigan city with largest Muslim population believe America should look more like Dearborn
item.description: Dearborn locals celebrate their city's diversity as Warren, Michigan residents worry about being pushed out as Muslim immigrants reshape their hometown.
item.content:encoded:
Residents of Dearborn, Michigan, a city with one of the nation's largest Muslim populations, told Fox News Digital that other cities should embrace diversity instead of fearing becoming "the next Dearborn."

"I hear intolerance when I hear something like that. I hear communities that don't understand what they're missing out on. They're missing out on culture," Diedo told Fox News Digital.

"They're missing out on awareness. I went to Dearborn Divine Child for high school, for grade school, for middle school – people that say that they are unfamiliar with what's coming and what's coming is going to be great y'all, so stand by for it," he added.

ABDUL EL-SAYED DELIVERS MAJOR BLOW TO GOP IN MICHIGAN AFTER BRUISING SENATE RACE

Jamal Jawad, owner of The Custard Company, told Fox News Digital that diversity is beneficial to the country.

"It's good to be diverse. You have people of different faiths, people of different cultures all over the place, all over the country. I mean it's good," Jawad said inside Toum, a new restaurant he was preparing to open in western Dearborn.

The nearby city of Warren, Michigan, another Detroit suburb, has also experienced demographic changes. The sale of a local church for conversion into the Al Ihsaan Islamic Center reflects one such change.

In Warren, several residents interviewed by Fox News Digital said they felt like they're being pushed out of their own hometown as Muslims immigrate to the area, expressing concerns about being the "next Dearborn."

Warren, Michigan's third-largest city after Detroit and Grand Rapids, grew rapidly during the post-World War II auto manufacturing boom, as war veterans moved to the area to work for Ford and General Motors. The blue-collar, white-picket-fence community incorporated as a city in 1957.

NYC'S MAMDANI SAYS ABDUL EL-SAYED'S SENATE VICTORY IN MICHIGAN 'MEANS SO MUCH TO SO MANY'

Dearborn residents embraced Muslim and Arab immigration to Michigan and rejected warnings about the area's changing demographics.

"That's bad. Come on, we gotta get past all that stuff," Dave Tilbot told Fox News Digital.

Another Dearborn resident, who did not disclose his name, said: "That is not an insult, it's actually a great thing, because I feel like the rest of America should be a little similar to Dearborn because it's a city, a beautiful city full of lots of people and all types of people: Mexican, Asian, Chinese, Arabic, American, Blacks."

"We got all types of people around here and it's a beautiful, beautiful city so I hope the world could become like Dearborn," he added.

JEWISH LEADERS IN MICHIGAN PREPARE TO WORK WITH ABDUL EL-SAYED DESPITE LINGERING CONCERNS

Ahmad Seif, a graduate of the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor who makes sushi for a living, told Fox News Digital that Dearborn is home to people from a variety of Arab backgrounds.

"I think ‘the next Dearborn’ is a big statement because there's never going to be a place like Dearborn where there's so many Arabs in one place … maybe like New York, but even then it's like Dearborn has so much different kinds of Arabs too," Seif said.

He added, "It's not just one kind like we have Yemenis, we have Lebanese, Syrian, Palestinian, Iraqis …"

Immigrants from Lebanon, Iraq and Syria began settling in the Detroit area in the early 20th century, drawn in part by growing demand for labor in the auto industry.

DEARBORN SCHOOLS APOLOGIZE AFTER 200-PLUS STUDENTS MISTAKENLY SERVED PORK DURING RAMADAN

Hala, a Dearborn resident, told Fox News Digital that Dearborn has the best food.

"I think that's the best compliment we could be ‘the next Dearborn’ who doesn't wanna be in Dearborn?" she asked.

Deronda Evans, an educator, told Fox News Digital that she views the prospect of another city becoming the "next Dearborn" positively.

"I hear something positive because Dearborn is developing and it's really multicultural. They have some good things going on, and some abandoned buildings are now businesses and have good choices, have good vibes, and I feel safe when I'm here," Evans said.

She went on to say, "I come here very often just to chill and enjoy myself, so I hear something positive because it's developing just like Detroit is developing."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed delivered a victory speech at an Arab America Foundation summit in Virginia shortly after Election Day, where he called Michigan the "capital of Arab America."

"I know we’re here in D.C., which, of course, is the capital of the United States of America. But Michigan is the capital of Arab America," El-Sayed said.

Dearborn Mayor Abdullah Hammoud told Fox News Digital this week what he thought El-Sayed meant by that statement.

"I think he's just speaking to the idea that the largest concentration of Arab Americans happens to be in the city of Dearborn, just [as] you have so many other cities across America celebrating the unique demographic, sometimes the largest of X population residing within their city bounds — no different," he said.

item.title: Zelenskyy presses US for expanded Russia talks as Kushner announces breakthrough
item.description: Jared Kushner said Russia agreed to multilateral Ukraine war talks involving Europe after Zelenskyy urged the Trump administration to move quickly.
item.content:encoded:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling on the U.S. to quickly organize talks with Russia with the full participation of European negotiators and advisors in what would mark a first-of-its-kind meeting.

He made the call Thursday after meeting with several U.S. and European leaders in Berlin at the Coalition of the Willing summit, which focused on security guarantees aimed at deterring future Russian aggression. During the meeting, U.S. special envoy Jared Kushner announced that Moscow and President Donald Trump had agreed to a multilateral negotiating format involving Europe.

"We are counting on the American side to help organize the first multilateral meeting at the team level, with full European participation, as soon as possible," Zelenskyy said.

The push signals an effort to prevent Europe and Kyiv from being sidelined in U.S.-Russia talks.

KUSHNER, WITKOFF SET FOR KYIV TALKS AFTER PUTIN MEETING IN US PUSH FOR PEACE

"From the very beginning, Ukraine has advocated for this approach — maximum coordination among us on everything concerning European and Ukrainian security and our future," Zelenskyy said.

"We need to work quickly, and this is the only approach Ukraine is taking. The more actively the discussions move forward, the greater the chances of achieving real progress."

According to Kushner, Russia agreed to the expanded negotiating format, including a recent breakthrough on prisoner exchanges.

"Russia has agreed to engage in the multilateral format with the Europeans. Part of that was us explaining to the Russians that we do believe that Russia having Europe at the table will be essential to ending this war in a just and long-term, durable way," Kushner said.

"There's going to be thousands of prisoners of war who will be going home to their families in the next weeks, which will be, obviously, a great gesture and a great relief for people."

FRENCH TROOPS SECRETLY DEPLOYED INSIDE UKRAINE AS EX-NATO CHIEF PRAISES MACRON'S 'GUTS'

He added that President Donald Trump will not impose a unilateral deal but will work with allies to finalize postwar security guarantees.

"President Trump wants to make a deal with Europe by his side. He's not looking to impose anything unilaterally," Kushner said.

"Our goal is really to end this war and to really help build a durable peace. We are very committed. President Trump will do whatever it takes to do that."

item.title: Hakeem Jeffries wins overwhelming Speaker-designate vote as progressives' revolt falls flat
item.description: House Democrats unified behind Hakeem Jeffries with 251 of 262 secret ballots as 11 progressive holdouts demanded votes on ICE, Gaza and Citizens United.
item.content:encoded:
Democrats are fretting that the "Bloc" of progressives will lug House Democrats to the left.

But, there is strength in numbers.

Yours truly wanted to understand just how much sway progressives might have over the House Democratic Caucus. Look no further than Wednesday morning’s vote for speaker.

No one challenged House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) to become speaker-designate in the internal caucus vote.

It’s about the math.

Jeffries marshaled 251 of the 262 secret ballots cast. The recorded vote revealed that despite all of their noise and clamor, extreme progressives really don’t have much juice compared to the rest of the Democratic Caucus. In fact, rank-and-file Democrats crushed their progressive colleagues.

Democrats did not vote by name. But numbers say a lot. While the recorded vote could have revealed potential craters of dissent among Democrats and questions about Jeffries, the tally registered the opposite. It showed just how diminutive the hard left is in the Democratic Caucus.

JEFFRIES BRUSHES OFF OPPOSITION FROM FAR-LEFT DEMS WHO VOTED NO: 'WE’RE GOING TO WORK TOGETHER'

Do they exude an outsized political voice? Yes. But success in Congress is measured in numbers. And at least on Wednesday, the numbers signaled few results for the Bloc and a show of unity among Democrats.

"With the majority as big as it is, it's going to be very hard for anybody to try and hold our group of hostage," forecast Rep. Tom Suozzi (D-N.Y.).

"We’re going to work together to find the highest common denominator in order to make life better for the American people," said Jeffries.

With more than 260 likely members in the Democratic Caucus, the Bloc wasn’t a factor on the first vote which mattered.

In January, Jeffries becomes the 57th person and the first Black speaker to grip the gavel. Members of the Congressional Black Caucus celebrated the ascendency of their colleague.

"I've been thinking about (the former Rep.) John Lewis (D-Ga.) a lot this week," said former House Majority Whip and Rep. Jim Clyburn (D-S.C.), invoking the civil rights figure. "This is a very surreal moment for me."

Clyburn spoke on behalf of Jeffries’ candidacy in the caucus, declaring that the path for the New York Democrat to the speakership makes him "feel vindicated."

"As a Black woman from the South, having the next speaker of the House to be a Black man means a lot to me," said Rep. Nikema Williams (D-Ga.).

Rep. Jonathan Jackson (D-Ill.) is the son of late Rev. Jesse Jackson. I asked what Jackson’s father would think of Jeffries rising to the speakership.

"He’d be more than happy to see America making progress. This is what the world looks like. This is what America looks like," said Jackson.

WATCH: JEFFRIES FACES UNCERTAINTY FROM INCOMING DEMOCRATS AS HOUSE SPEAKER VOTE APPROACHES

But let’s filet the caucus vote for speaker to understand what unfolded with 11 Democrats who withheld their support from Jeffries.

Representative-elect Don Leonard (D-Ohio) is a populist in a district which President Trump won by 10 points in 2024. Leonard defeated Rep. Mike Carey (R-Ohio). The district Leonard flipped in central Ohio is a long way politically from left-leaning districts in New York City and New Jersey where renegade members of the Bloc refused to cast their ballots for Jeffries.

"What we need is a commitment from the speaker to get a 28th Amendment passed in 2028, to end Citizens United, end the corruption and call a vote on U.S. military aid to Israel," said Leonard. "If he does those things, he's got my vote."

Seven of the progressives published a joint statement, demanding commitments from Jeffries to stop ICE and end "genocide in Gaza."

The seven declared they saw "meaningful progress" in their talks with Jeffries. But since those negotiations continue, "our vote in caucus today was no" against Jeffries.

Despite repeated efforts, none of the seven spoke to Fox.

But what’s remarkable is that two of the seven withholding their support hail from Jeffries’ hometown, New York City. One is Representative-elect Claire Valdez (D-N.Y.) — who will represent a wide swath of Brooklyn and Queens. The other is Representative-elect Darializa Avila Chevalier (D-N.Y.). That district comprises parts of Upper Manhattan and The Bronx.

Your trusty reporter tried to understand what the dissent meant.

"How are their districts different than yours, being next door?" I asked Jeffries.

He deflected.

"The numbers speak for themselves," said Jeffries.

I tried again.

"But those districts — are they that different from what you represent? And yet they weren't willing to vote for you, Mr. speaker-designate?"

No response.

The lack of support for Jeffries from the dissidents annoyed Rep. Marilyn Strickland (D-Wash.).

"This idea that Hakeem Jeffries has not earned this is completely absurd. He has worked hard. He's done everything he needed to do," said Strickland.

Rep. Nydia Velázquez (D-N.Y.) is retiring at the end of this Congress. She opposed Valdez as her successor. She was bewildered that Valdez and Avila Chevalier wouldn’t support their hometown, Big Apple Congressman for speaker.

"My advice to them is take the time to know how this institution runs and what it takes to be successful here," said an agitated Velázquez.

Rep. Joe Morelle (D-N.Y.) served with Jeffries in the state legislature. He argued that Valdez and Avila Chevalier made a mistake.

"They’re going to have to answer to their constituents," said Morelle. "I think they should have been with Hakeem Jeffries who’s led us to this historic majority."

And if you aren’t on the team in politics, the team also isn’t on you.

"It is a small group that marginalized themselves," said Rep. Henry Cuellar (D-Texas) about the holdouts.

However, Representative-elect Dan Koh (D-Mass.) saw it differently.

"They all got elected with very different constituencies. A lot of them have different priorities," said Koh. "There are things that their constituencies have demanded. And they want to make sure have the audience of the leader."

Rep. Greg Landsman (D-Ohio) believed there was strategy in the dissent.

"They probably chose to do this because it's a way of lifting up their issues," said Landsman.

And keep in mind, this wasn’t the actual vote for speaker. That comes on the floor in January. It’s a win-win for Jeffries and the holdouts if they forge an accord. He promises them certain votes. And they can then tout what they extracted from the next speaker.

This is politics.

But let’s put the 11 defections into context.

Democrats flipped the House in 2018. In the internal caucus election, former House Speaker Nancy Pelosi (D-Calif.) lost 32 votes. In the vote for speaker in January 2019, 12 Democrats voted for someone else. Three members voted present.

"Nancy Pelosi will be remembered," said Rep. Jared Moskowitz (D-Fla.). "And the 30 people who voted against her will not be remembered."

Jeffries will go down in the history books as the first Black speaker. The holdouts? They’re freshmen. As Moskowitz suggests, we’ll see if anyone recalls them in a few years.

item.title: Sarah Huckabee Sanders recalls ‘jarring’ encounter with angry mom who spat on her car
item.description: Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders recalled a mom yelling in her face and spitting on her car at pre-K drop-off, a moment she says left her in shock.
item.content:encoded:
Arkansas Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders recalled a "jarring" verbal assault she experienced at the hands of an angry mother while serving as White House press secretary during the first Trump administration.

Sanders, who served as President Donald Trump’s White House press secretary from 2017 to 2019, relived an incident in which a mother berated her and spit on her car as she dropped off her toddler at school.

"I was walking my youngest son into his pre-K class, and as I was going in, I'm holding his hand, another mom who has a child that's a 2- or 3-year-old in my son's class, kinda yells in my face, tells me what an awful human I am while standing next to my child and then turns and spits on our car," she said on a new episode of "Hang Out with Sean Hannity."

MAHER CHALLENGES SARAH HUCKABEE SANDERS ON 'SOCIALISM' AS ARKANSAS GOVERNOR DEFENDS FREE SCHOOL BREAKFASTS

The newly re-elected Arkansas governor said she had never been so "angry" and "disgusted," particularly because the woman scolded her in front of her toddler and other young children.

"I was so, just, like, in shock. I'd never experienced something like that," she said. "It was so ... jarring and off-putting."

Sanders, whose father, Mike Huckabee, serves as U.S. ambassador to Israel, said the encounter was among several difficult experiences she endured while working for Trump. She offered a glimpse into the price she paid working for the president during an especially politically contentious period.

DANA PERINO SHARES HOW SHE SECRETLY PUSHED BACK AT REPORTERS DURING WHITE HOUSE BRIEFINGS

During her final year in the administration, Sanders said she rarely ventured beyond the Trump International Hotel (now known as the Waldorf Astoria Washington DC) in Washington, D.C., which she described as a refuge from hostility she encountered elsewhere. She said she often feared restaurants would tamper with her food.

"It was the only place that we could go and not get screamed at, or yelled at, or flipped off," Sanders said, saying the role of press secretary was the "hardest" job she ever had.

"We could always get a table, and the food was good, and the people were nice and we knew they weren't spitting in our food," she added.

Despite the hostility she encountered from critics of Trump, Sanders said she also experienced numerous positive interactions with people who commended her work in the administration. The governor said those interactions made the hard days "worth it."

"Thankfully, for every one of those there were a hundred moments of people who would come up and say, ‘Thank you for standing with the president,’" Sanders said.

item.title: NWSL boss says all fans are 'welcome' ahead of final after multiple ejections of women's sports advocates
item.description: NWSL Commissioner Jessica Berman says fans of all viewpoints are "100% welcome" as Jennifer Sey will attend the final wearing XX-XY Athletics apparel.
item.content:encoded:
National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) Commissioner Jessica Berman said fans are "100% welcome" to come to the league's game regardless of their viewpoints as "Save Women's Sports" advocates prepare to attend the championship game on Saturday.

Still, Berman defended clubs’ discretion in enforcing league policies amid disputes involving spectators who oppose transgender participation in women’s sports, as spectators sporting gear that advocates for the protection of women's sports have been ejected from multiple NWSL games this season.

Berman addressed the issue Thursday ahead of Saturday’s championship in Washington, D.C., where XX-XY Athletics founder Jennifer Sey plans to attend with former NWSL player Elizabeth Eddy and other friends wearing her brand’s apparel.

"We expect the people who come into our buildings, no matter their points of view, to be there to enjoy the excitement and the incredible athleticism of our players and the competition on the field," Berman said. "And if people are there for that reason, they are 100% welcome."

FORMER NWSL PLAYER SAYS LEAGUE CULTURE PRESSURED ATHLETES TO SUPPORT POLITICAL MESSAGES THEY OPPOSED

"And it’s our job to make sure that we enforce those policies consistently across all of our stadiums," she added.

The comments came in response to a question about potential conflicts involving spectators who oppose transgender players’ participation and established supporters’ groups.

Berman began by calling supporters’ groups "the lifeblood of this league," emphasizing their contribution to the atmosphere at matches.

Asked whether handling such incidents should be a league or club responsibility, Berman described a "hybrid approach."

"There is a league policy in place that creates an umbrella of minimum standards that we expect that is our responsibility to enforce," she said. "And then we leave it up to the individual clubs to decide what makes sense in their local market because there are unique attributes of particular communities that we may not be aware of."

Berman did not name Sey or XX-XY Athletics during that exchange or announce a restriction on the brand’s apparel.

Sey said no one from the league had contacted her about her attendance as of the interview. Her concern about being denied entry was not based on a restriction communicated to her by the NWSL.

"I bought these tickets weeks ago. I’m not changing my plans," she added. "We have every right to be there."

'SAVE WOMEN’S SPORTS' ACTIVISTS EJECTED FROM NWSL MATCH AFTER BEING STRUCK, CONFRONTED BY PRO-TRANS CROWD

Asked whether she feared being turned away, Sey said she was concerned but would not change her plans.

"I dare you to not let me in. I promise you, I will be a peaceful attendee. I’m there to watch the game. If my shirt bothers you, look the other way," she said.

Her planned attendance follows separate disputes involving spectators wearing XX-XY Athletics apparel at Portland Thorns matches.

On Sept. 6, spectators were removed from Providence Park during a match against the Washington Spirit. Members of the group said they were removed over their apparel, while the Thorns said they had distributed unapproved materials in violation of stadium guidelines. The group disputed the club’s explanation.

A separate October incident involved commentator Brandi Kruse and other spectators who said they were forcibly removed because they wore the brand’s shirts.

Sey disputed the suggestion that wearing her company’s logo inherently constitutes provocation, citing other sporting events she said she attended without significant problems.

"We’re the women’s sports fans," she said. "We’re going to watch the game. Ignore us if you don’t like it."

She said fans expressing support for transgender inclusion should also be allowed to wear their apparel.

"I can ignore them and enjoy the game anyway," Sey said. "They can ignore me."

Asked what she wanted to hear from the commissioner, Sey said: "I would like her to say all soccer fans are welcome. All women’s sports fans are welcome. It’s that simple."

Sey said Eddy accepted her invitation immediately and had not expressed reservations about attending. She also said her daughter plays travel soccer and that she was particularly excited to watch Washington Spirit star Trinity Rodman.

The Spirit face the Kansas City Current at Audi Field on Saturday.

Asked how she would respond if security requested that she leave, Sey said she would remain calm and ask why.

"I won’t just accept being ejected," she said, describing her intended response as "peaceful protest."

OutKick reached out to the NWSL asking whether Sey and her guests would be allowed to enter and remain at the championship wearing XX-XY Athletics apparel, and whether objections from other fans could lead to their removal. OutKick also asked what policies govern those decisions, how security would respond to harassment directed at the group and whether the league wished to respond to Sey’s comments. The NWSL had not responded by publication time.

item.title: ASRA Q. NOMANI: Inside the coordinated activist blitz that crashed Anthropic’s historic Nasdaq debut
item.description: As Anthropic rang the Nasdaq opening bell in Times Square, NYPD zip-tied four protesters who blocked the doors with linked arms and pre-printed banners.
item.content:encoded:
As Anthropic executives gathered inside the Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square on Thursday morning to ring the opening bell for a historic $81 billion initial public offering, a tightly orchestrated coalition of far-left, socialist, environmental, anti-Israel and Democratic grassroots groups executed a staged street action outside, complete with linked-arm sit-ins, pre-printed banners and rapid-fire social media drops timed to hijack the news cycle.

"This IPO has got to go! Hey, hey, ho, ho," the staged protesters chanted to a small cadre of photographers as the audience.

"Shame! Shame!" a protester yelled to a few responding "Shame!" in response.

item.title: Washington voters protected women’s sports. ACLU wants to overturn democracy
item.description: Washington state voters passed Initiative 638 to protect women's sports, but the ACLU's lawsuit now threatens to overturn their more than 10-point margin.
item.content:encoded:
I ran a lot of track for many years. I’m fast enough that, back in high school, I was named Female Track & Field Athlete of the Year three years in a row by my school’s coaching staff.

But I’m not a male. Male athletes have strength and speed I’ll never have, and when I step out on the track, forced to run against one, I know, before the pistol even fires, that the result is already decided—we’re just going through the motions. Voters in four states—red and blue—understood this when they went to the ballot box on Nov. 3 and passed measures protecting women's sports. Now the American Civil Liberties Union is seeking to undo the one in Washington state.

Other female athletes and I won’t take this without a fight, because we speak from experience. In one of my best high school events—the girls' 4x400-meter relay race—my relay team ran against a male athlete who had previously competed in the high school boys' category. He beat us, easily, and went on to beat a lot of other girls. He even won the state championship in the women’s 400-meter race two years in a row.

ACLU OF WASHINGTON SAYS IT WILL SUE TO BLOCK BALLOT INITIATIVE TO PROTECT GIRLS' SPORTS

No female athlete runs to lose, any more than a male does. We didn’t put ourselves through all that rigorous training, grind through those straining workouts or run those endless sprints for the fun of watching someone else finish race after race ahead of us.

When males enter girls’ sports, that’s not competition. Running races you’re guaranteed to win is not competition; neither is entering races you’re guaranteed to lose. All these male athletes are doing is securing automatic trophies for themselves while women like me lose roster spots, records, medals, our turn on the podium, and our privacy.

WASHINGTON AG'S OFFICE INDICATES IT WILL DEFEND GIRLS' SPORTS BALLOT MEASURE AFTER ACLU SUES TO BLOCK IT

Years ago, Congress passed Title IX to ensure that wouldn’t happen. Earlier this month, seeing that social and political movements had combined to undercut that landmark law, Washington state voters, Democrats and Republicans alike, rallied to pass Initiative 638—by a margin of more than 10 percentage points—to vindicate Title IX and protect women's sports.

Voters had to do that; our legislators wouldn’t. But then, our voters understand what our elected representatives can’t seem to grasp: that biology isn’t red or blue. This is not a partisan issue—it’s common sense. And it’s up to the state of Washington to defend in court what a clear majority of its citizens have made law at the ballot box.

WASHINGTON PARENTS FIND THEIR COURAGE AS GIRLS WALK OFF CROSS COUNTRY COURSE IN PROTEST OF TRANS RUNNER

We need our officials to step up, because the ACLU—unable to make its case that men should be in women’s sports at the ballot box—is demanding that a state court go around us and overturn Initiative 638. To ensure the ACLU doesn't succeed, Alliance Defending Freedom is representing Female Athletes United, a coalition of female athletes, in filing a motion to intervene in the ACLU’s lawsuit. I’m filing a declaration as part of that lawsuit.

I’ve been here before. Last year, I filed a complaint with the U.S. Department of Education’s Office for Civil Rights, asking it to investigate our state’s athletic policies and require that sex-designated sports categories be based on sex. I did that not only for myself but for countless other young women across my state who’ve been on the receiving end of this issue for years—and for our younger sisters, waiting to take their own blows for the cause.

This isn’t about wounded pride. It’s about safety: another female athlete in our state, Kallie Keeler, for instance, suffered great harm during a high school women’s wrestling match against a competitor who turned out to be male. None of the coaches or officials had bothered to tell her.

It’s also about privacy: Would you want your daughter changing clothes and showering with men who’ve politicized their way into her locker room?

And it’s about fairness. A United Nations report documents more than 600 female athletes across 29 sports who’ve been displaced by men; the men collectively took more than 890 medals. But then, just in West Virginia, one male defeated more than 470 girls over 1,400 times in a single sport.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

That’s the instance that resulted in last summer’s State of West Virginia v. B.P.J. case, in which the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that states can protect women’s sports. Twenty-seven states have passed legislation to do just that; in this month’s midterm elections, voters in Arizona, Colorado, Nebraska, and Washington joined them.

Now we know where the public stands on this issue. We hope the state officials who failed us once are going to step up this time to stand with us. But we’re not waiting to find out.

item.title: ‘Stand your ground’ claim falters in road rage killing as men charged with murder, ex-cops face accusations
item.description: Two South Carolina men face murder charges in Scott Spivey's road rage death after his sister uncovered recordings that sank their "stand your ground" defense.
item.content:encoded:
Two South Carolina men have been charged with murder in the road rage shooting death of a man whose sister uncovered evidence that the slaying was not self-defense as originally claimed. And two former police officers involved in the investigation are facing accusations of official misconduct.

Scott Spivey, a 33-year-old insurance adjuster from North Carolina, died Sept. 9, 2023, after a car chase on Highway 9 in Horry County led to his shooting death on Camp Swamp Road, 9 miles away.

Charles "Weldon" Boyd and Kenneth "Bradley" Williams had originally invoked the state's "stand your ground" law and argued they were defending themselves from an irrational driver. They were both arrested Wednesday, more than three years after the incident.

SECRET TAPES SINK SHOOTER'S DEFENSE IN SCOTT SPIVEY ROAD RAGE KILLING

Brandon Strickland and Paul Vescovi, a former deputy chief and sergeant with the Horry County Police Department, also face charges, including misconduct in office and obstruction of justice, according to local reports. Strickland, who allegedly spoke with Boyd on the phone after the shooting, was also charged with criminal conspiracy. 

All four made initial appearances in criminal court Thursday afternoon. The judge did not rule on their bond requests at the end of the two-hour hearing, according to the Myrtle Beach-based WMBF-TV. Separate decisions were expected to be posted later.

At the time of the shooting, Spivey, Boyd and Williams were all armed, according to court documents. Spivey eventually pulled over, got out of his vehicle and screamed at Boyd and Williams to stop following him. The pursuers allegedly opened fire and killed him in what his sister's attorney described as "a hail of gunfire" in a wrongful death lawsuit.

Spivey's sister, Jennifer Spivey Foley, uncovered recordings from Boyd's phone buried in the police case file that had previously not been made public or factored into the case, and The Wall Street Journal published them last year, bringing national attention to the case.

Foley attended the hearing Thursday and asked the judge to deny bond for both Boyd and Williams and to order a mental health evaluation for Boyd.

According to court documents in the Spivey family's wrongful death case, the recordings indicate that Boyd told a 911 dispatcher that Spivey was "trying to get away" and nevertheless was prepared for a shootout.

"If I see the gun again, I'm going to take the motherf----- down," Boyd allegedly told the dispatcher, according to the civil complaint in a wrongful death lawsuit filed in 2024.

Boyd remained on the line until the shooting took place, according to the wrongful death lawsuit.

Later, according to the Journal report, he allegedly called his friend, who was Horry County's deputy police chief at the time.

Defense filings in the civil case allege that Spivey had pointed a pistol at Williams' head and ran Boyd's truck off the road at the start of the encounter. In a 911 call, a man identified as Boyd told the dispatcher that the other driver shot first. 

O’Bryan Martin, an attorney for Williams, disputed the idea that the shooting was anything other than self-defense.

In court documents in the civil case, lawyers for Boyd and Williams have accused Spivey of being the aggressor by pointing a gun at Williams through the window without provocation. 

Martin said that other drivers called 911 to report similarly erratic behavior before Spivey ran into Boyd’s truck on the highway.

"When you're claiming self-defense, we always have to analyze, first and foremost: Well, who brought on the difficulty? Who caused this to start? Who started the fight, to boil it down? Boyd and Williams' lawyers had filed for a stay of proceedings in the civil case on Nov. 5, citing a pending grand jury inquiry, court records show. Within days, their clients were indicted.

"For over three years, Scott Spivey’s family has fought for something that should never have required a fight — the truth about how and why Scott was killed," Mark Tinsley, the attorney representing the victim's family, wrote in a statement posted to Facebook. 

"From the beginning, this family has believed that Scott’s death was not justified."

The criminal case is being handled by a special prosecutor after local prosecutors had declined to file criminal charges.

"The tragedy of this case is not just that Scott Spivey lost his life," Tinsley added. "It is that his family had to fight the very system that was supposed to investigate his death to get to the truth."

item.content:encoded:

Imagine trying to get a shot off, but instead of thinking about your mechanics, your brain starts short-circuiting because, unless you have a sub-par GPA and they dug it up, there's no reason for it.

item.title: Puka Nacua is suspended by the NFL but discipline's timing could not have been any better for Rams receiver
item.description: Puka Nacua's three-game NFL suspension lands while the Los Angeles Rams star sits on injured reserve, costing game checks but no actual games.
item.content:encoded:
Puka Nacua just got one of the most fortuitously timed, if not one of the most toothless, NFL suspensions in recent memory.

The NFL announced on Thursday that Nacua has been suspended for the Los Angeles Rams next three games without pay for violating the league's Personal Conduct Policy.

The suspension begins immediately and Nacua will be eligible for reinstatement Monday, Dec. 14 following the Rams’ game against the San Francisco 49ers.

RAMS STAR PUKA NACUA OUT FOR AN 'EXTENDED PERIOD' AFTER SUFFERING INJURY ON FINAL PLAY OF WIN

The amazing timing of this suspension, beyond the fact it comes in November and not at the start of the season, is that it happens while Nacua is on injured reserve list and could not play in the games he's suspended anyway because he nursing an MCL in his right knee as well as a turf toe injury.

Nacua suffered those injuries in the Nov. 8 victory over the Washington Commanders and was placed on the injured reserve list on Nov. 12.

NFL rules related to injured reserve say a player on IR must miss four games before being eligible to return.

That meant Nacua had sit out at least four games while on injured reserve, at the Arizona Cardinals, which already happened, at home against the Green Bay Packers and Kansas City Chiefs, and at the San Francisco 49ers on Dec. 13.

NFL'S CONDUCT POLICY REVIEW OF PUKA NACUA CONTINUES AND THAT DRIVES FANTASY FOOTBALL MANAGERS NUTS

Amazingly, the suspension announced on Thursday and Nacua's stint on the injured reserve list both run to Dec. 13 and he can return from both on Dec. 14.

A player's injury designation does not delay discipline or prevent a suspension from being served, according to the NFL. So the suspension begins when it is imposed.

This means Nacua is basically being fined rather than suspended. The suspension for violating the Personal Conduct Policy will cost Nacua three game checks but no actual games because he's not able to play anyway.

The cost of not being paid versus being on IR and getting paid is not a small amount. The approximate amount the suspension will cost Nacua is $961,166,000.

But as to in-game value and ability to help the Rams, this suspension serves Nacua and the Rams perfectly.

The NFL has been reviewing Nacua's conduct since March when a civil lawsuit was filed against him in Los Angeles.

The NFL investigation probably centered on several key details and developments:

NFL SUSPENDS AND FINES 49ERS OWNER JED YORK FOR VIOLATION OF CONDUCT POLICY TIED TO PROSTITUTION ARREST

Nacua seemingly emerges from this ugly episode with something of a best-case scenario, albeit a financially costly one. But even on that score, he's probably coming out ahead.

item.title: One wild Week 11 betting stat shows just how far apart the NFL’s best and worst teams are
item.description: Two NFL teams could win by two touchdowns Sunday and still not cover, as Week 11 spreads hit their highest average since 1999, per BetMGM odds.
item.content:encoded:
Two NFL teams could win by two touchdowns Sunday and still fail to cover. We're used to seeing that sort of thing on a Saturday in September, when somebody’s getting a nice check to go play an SEC or Big Ten team.

Instead, it's happening in the NFL in Week 11. Of the 13 games, five feature a team laying double digits and nine have a team laying at least six points, according to BetMGM odds on Thursday afternoon.

WHICH NFL TEAMS CAN ACTUALLY WIN THE SUPER BOWL? RANKING ALL 32 AT THE SEASON’S HALFWAY POINT

The 8-1 Bills are favored by 16.5 points at home against the 1-8 Dolphins. The 7-2 Chiefs are 15.5-point home favorites against the 3-7 Cardinals. Those are the two biggest numbers, but they aren't alone. The 3-6 (!) Texans are 12.5-point home favorites against the Colts on Thursday Night Football, and the 7-2 Bears are laying 11.5 points at home against the 3-6 Saints.

The average closing spread through the first 10 weeks of this season was 4.71 points. On Thursday, the 13 games on BetMGM Week 11 board averaged a whopping 8.2-point spread differential.

I went back to 1999 using nflverse’s closing lines and threw out the final two weeks of each season, when teams with their playoff seeding locked up are more likely to rest starters. That left 420 completed weeks, and none had a closing average as high as Thursday’s board. The highest closing average in that sample was 7.75 points in Week 12 of 2007.

That was the week the undefeated Patriots were favored by 24 against the Eagles. They won by three, by the way.

It’s easy to see why Buffalo and Kansas City are favored by more than two touchdowns. Just look at the starting quarterbacks. The Bills, led by 2024 NFL MVP Josh Allen, face Miami’s Kyle McCord, a sixth-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft making his second career start.

The Chiefs and two-time MVP Patrick Mahomes get Arizona’s Carson Beck, a rookie third-round pick who’s also making his second career start.

Injuries have played a massive role in widening the quarterback gap across the NFL. Miami put Malik Willis on injured reserve, forcing McCord into action. Beck was Arizona’s emergency third quarterback a few weeks ago, but the Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore and lost Gardner Minshew to injury.

The Ravens needed Brissett because Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley are both on injured reserve. And since putting Jalen Hurts on injured reserve, the Eagles have turned to Tanner McKee and now Joe Milton, who’s starting against Pittsburgh on Sunday. The Steelers might need to do some soul-searching since Aaron Rodgers' squad is just a 4.5-point favorite on the road against Milton and the Eagles.

Look, no one likes seeing referees flag defenders for seemingly normal football tackles made on quarterbacks (except maybe the quarterbacks). Those 15-yard roughing-the-passer fouls can save drives, change games, and frustrate fans. But it's also pretty clear why rules exist to protect quarterbacks.

Star quarterbacks are not only the faces of the league and paid hundreds of millions of dollars, but their presence on the field objectively makes the product better.

The Colts traded Quenton Nelson, Josh Downs and Keenan Allen in the run-up to the deadline, and I get why a three-win team wants draft picks. It’s a tough sell in Indianapolis, though, where the Colts have made the playoffs just once since Andrew Luck retired and last won a playoff game after the 2018 regular season, Luck’s last. They finally fired GM Chris Ballard in October after nearly a decade on the job.

But playoff futility certainly isn't unique to the Colts. The Dolphins haven’t won a playoff game since 2000, and the Cardinals last won one in the 2015 season. The Jets haven’t even made the playoffs since the 2010 season.

DESPITE COMPLAINTS ABOUT OTHER SPORTS, THE NFL HAS BECOME THE MOST PREDICTABLE LEAGUE IN AMERICA

New York faces the 1-8 Chargers this week, and Los Angeles is favored. The Chargers have won a single playoff game since moving from San Diego to Los Angeles in 2017.

Other teams facing large spreads this week haven't been competitive in years. The Saints haven't made the playoffs in the past five seasons. The Raiders, who are 10-point underdogs at Denver, last won a playoff game in the 2002 season. The Titans, 8-point dogs at the Cowboys, have finished last in the AFC South in each of the past three seasons and are on their way to another basement finish this year.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

But it's not just about bad teams failing to make the playoffs; there's also a lack of parity among teams competing to win Super Bowls.

Only 11 teams reached the Super Bowl across the 2013 through 2025 seasons, and the Patriots, Chiefs, Seahawks and Eagles won 10 of the 13 titles. Buffalo and Cincinnati each reached the AFC Championship Game twice in that 13-season span, with the Bengals winning the conference after the 2021 season.

Every AFC Championship Game since Steelers–Jets in January 2011 has featured the Patriots or the Chiefs. Thirteen NFC teams reached their conference title game over the past 13 seasons, but the Seahawks, Eagles, 49ers and Rams won 10 of those games.

We’ll see if this season ends any differently. San Francisco and Buffalo are both 8-1, with Kansas City and Cincinnati right behind at 7-2, so I wouldn’t count on seeing a whole lot of new faces in January.

On Sunday, the Bills and Chiefs are laying a combined 32 points in two games. I’ll have all four TVs going for the early games, and I hope I still need all four by halftime.
